images.caption: Figure 2:WorldLatent training pipeline. (a) WorldVAE training: Multiple 4D spatiotemporal modalities, including monocular RGB video, depth maps, and camera Plücker coordinates (ray direction𝐝\mathbf{d}and moment𝐦\mathbf{m}), are compressed via modality-specific encoders (E1E_{1}–E4E_{4}) and fused by a Dense Prediction Transformer (DPT) into a unified latent bottleneck,𝐳4d\mathbf{z}_{\text{4d}}(WorldLatent). Modality-specific decoders (D1D_{1}–D4D_{4}) then reconstruct the original modalities from this shared latent space. (b) Any-to-4D generative modeling: With the WorldVAE frozen, a unified diffusion model is trained within the learned latent space. It takes Gaussian noise, text prompts (CtextC_{\text{text}}), and partial or empty 4D latents𝐜4d​(𝒮)\mathbf{c}_{\text{4d}}(\mathcal{S})(e.g.,𝒮=∅\mathcal{S}=\varnothingfor text-to-4D generation, RGB-only for perception, or depth-only for editing) to synthesize the full 4D latent𝐳4d\mathbf{z}_{\text{4d}}. Finally, the frozen decoders (D1D_{1}–D4D_{4}) map𝐳4d\mathbf{z}_{\text{4d}}back into temporally coherent video, 3D geometry, and camera trajectories.

Figure 3:Qualitative comparison of zero-shot video depth estimation.Results are shown across the MPI Sintel, Bonn, and ScanNet datasets. For each clip, we display the input RGB frames, ground-truth depth, predictions from the teacher model (DA3-Giant) and WorldLatent-14B (Ours).

Figure 4:Any-to-4D: world editing and depth-conditioned re-rendering with WorldLatent.(1) Given an input RGB video, our model first performs 4D perception to estimate dense depth maps. (2) Conditioned on these predicted depth maps and new text prompts, the same model then performs 4D re-rendering to synthesize appearance-edited RGB videos. For each example, we show the input video, the predicted depth and camera outputs from our 4D perception stage, and the re-rendered videos across diverse text prompts.

Figure 5:Any-to-4D: text-to-4D world generation with WorldLatent. Given only a text prompt, our model jointly denoises appearance, depth, and camera rays from noise, producing an RGB video together with aligned depth maps and a 3D scene with camera trajectory.
